bibl.title: SCANPY: large-scale single-cell gene expression data analysis

person.p: the tag layer; a sentence written by the tagger about the paper, always anchored to a quotation but not itself a quotation

span.label: single-cell gene expression data at a scale existing frameworks do not reach
span.quote: However, these frameworks do not scale to the increasingly available large data sets with up to and more than one million cells. Here, we present a framework that overcomes this limitation and provides similar analysis possibilities.

span.label: how to give the established single-cell analyses a form that scales past a million cells
span.quote: However, these frameworks do not scale to the increasingly available large data sets with up to and more than one million cells. Here, we present a framework that overcomes this limitation and provides similar analysis possibilities.

span.label: SCANPY, and ANNDATA - a generic annotated data matrix that every tool reads and writes without changing its structure
span.quote: With SCANPY , we introduce the class ANNDATA —with a corresponding package ANNDATA —which stores a data matrix with the most general annotations possible: annotations of observations (samples, cells) and variables (features, genes), and unstructured annotations.

span.label: method
span.quote: However, these frameworks do not scale to the increasingly available large data sets with up to and more than one million cells. Here, we present a framework that overcomes this limitation and provides similar analysis possibilities.

span.label: analysis frameworks failing at data sizes their science has already reached
span.quote: However, these frameworks do not scale to the increasingly available large data sets with up to and more than one million cells. Here, we present a framework that overcomes this limitation and provides similar analysis possibilities.

span.label: a Python toolkit built around one annotated data class, with HDF5 backing and a single reused neighbourhood graph
span.term: a Python toolkit built around one annotated data class, with HDF5 backing and a single reused neighbourhood graph
span.quote: Typically, SCANPY ’s tools reuse a once-computed, single graph representation of data and hence, avoid the use of different, potentially inconsistent, and computationally expensive representations of data.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: ONE REPRESENTATION, COMPUTED ONCE, REUSED: the tools share a single graph of the data instead of each building its own, which the paper justifies by what it avoids - DIFFERENT, POTENTIALLY INCONSISTENT representations of the same data
span.quote: Typically, SCANPY ’s tools reuse a once-computed, single graph representation of data and hence, avoid the use of different, potentially inconsistent, and computationally expensive representations of data.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: EXTENSIBILITY THROUGH A FIXED STRUCTURE: a tool extracts from the matrix and writes its result back into the same object, and the object's structure is unaffected - so adding a method does not oblige anything else to change
span.quote: As SCANPY is built around that class, it is easy to add new functionality to the toolkit. All statistics and machine-learning tools extract information from a data matrix, which can be added to an ANNDATA object while leaving the structure of ANNDATA unaffected.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: SCALE BY CHANGING RESIDENCY, NOT ALGORITHM: HDF5 backing lets the object be operated on without being loaded, so the limit moves from memory size to disk
span.quote: This allows operating on an ANNDATA object without fully loading it into memory—the functionality is offered via ANNDATA ’s backed mode as opposed to its memory mode.

span.label: mechanisms
span.term: SPEED FROM BLOCKING, NOT FROM APPROXIMATION: neighbourhood distances are computed by aggregating rows into submatrices and multiplying, rather than by sampling
span.quote: The computation of neighborhood relations is much faster than in the popular reference package [ 27 ]. This is achieved by aggregating rows (observations) in a data matrix to submatrices and computing distances for each submatrix using fast parallelized matrix multiplication.

span.label: The comparison offered is against R-based frameworks and CELL RANGER; the claim of no comparable toolkit is scoped to the PYTHON ecosystem, in the paper's own words
span.quote: SCANPY integrates well into the existing Python ecosystem, in which no comparable toolkit yet exists.

span.label: The scaling evidence is a demonstration on named datasets - 68,579 cells for the speedup and 1.3 million for feasibility - not a complexity result
span.quote: Moreover, we demonstrate the feasibility of analyzing 1.3 million cells without subsampling in a few hours of computing time on eight cores of a small computing server

span.label: benchmarking SCANPY against established single-cell analysis packages on a clustering tutorial of 2,700 peripheral blood mononuclear cells
span.note: eliminates: that SCANPY's clustering results differ from what the established tools produce on the same data, so that its speed advantage comes at a cost in output · outcome: held
span.quote: SCANPY is benchmarked in comparisons with established packages In a detailed clustering tutorial of 2700 peripheral blood mononuclear cells (PBMCs), adapted from one of SEURAT ’s tutorials ( http://satijalab.org/seurat/pbmc3k_tutorial.html ) [ 2 ], all steps starting from raw count data to the identification of cell types are carried out, providing speedups between 5 and 90 times in each step ( https://github.com/theislab/scanpy_usage/tree/master/170505_seurat ).

span.label: EXPRESSIONSET
span.quote: ANNDATA is similar to R’s EXPRESSIONSET [ 26 ], but supports sparse data and allows HDF5-based backing of ANNDATA objects on disk, a format independent of platform, framework, and language.

span.label: CELL RANGER
span.quote: Benchmarking against the more run-time optimized CELL RANGER R kit [ 6 ], we demonstrate a speedup of 5 to 16 times for a data set of 68,579 PBMCs

span.label: SEURAT
span.quote: Simple integrated analysis work flows for single-cell transcriptomic data [ 1 ] have been enabled by frameworks such as SEURAT [ 2 ], MONOCLE [ 3 ], SCDE/PAGODA [ 4 ], MAST [ 5 ], CELL RANGER [ 6 ], SCATER [ 7 ], and SCRAN [ 8 ]. However, these frameworks do not scale to the increasingly available large data sets with up to and more than one million cells. Here, we present a framework that overcomes this limitation and provides similar analysis possibilities.

span.label: Python ecosystem
span.quote: SCANPY integrates well into the existing Python ecosystem, in which no comparable toolkit yet exists.

span.label: ANNDATA - THE ANNOTATION IS THE POINT, NOT THE MATRIX: a data matrix plus annotations of observations, of variables, and unstructured ones, held together so a tool can add a result without changing the structure everything else reads
span.quote: With SCANPY , we introduce the class ANNDATA —with a corresponding package ANNDATA —which stores a data matrix with the most general annotations possible: annotations of observations (samples, cells) and variables (features, genes), and unstructured annotations.
